entries.title: keep the simulator's last packets in the runner's pcaps
entries.body: The network simulator's run.sh forwarded the stop signal to dumpcap at once and then exited as PID 1. As a result, the packets of the last libpcap TPACKET_V3 block never reached the pcap. The ngtcp2 handshake case closes within about 80 ms, so its server trace had no QUIC packets, and the runner failed it with "Expected exactly one version. Got []". The workflow now builds the pinned simulator with run.sh patched so it waits 0.5 s before forwarding the signal and waits for dumpcap to exit.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: remove Arena.release, Arena.reset, --wrapping and --unchecked-indexing
entries.body:
* feat(checker)!: remove Arena.release, Arena.reset, --wrapping and --unchecked-indexing

The four deprecated ways to step around a check are gone before 1.0.

`Arena.release(m)` and `Arena.reset()` freed to a mark with no proof that
nothing allocated after it was still reachable. Each is now an unknown builtin
(NL2244); scope memory with `using a = arena()`. `Arena.mark` and `Arena.used`
stay, and a function that calls `Arena.mark` still takes no automatic arena
scope of its own.

`--wrapping` and `--unchecked-indexing` turned a check off for a whole
package. The CLI now refuses each with exit 2, as it already refused `--nsw`,
and names the per-site replacement from `nish:unsafe`: `wrappingAdd`,
`wrappingSub` and `wrappingMul`, or `uncheckedGet` and `uncheckedSet`. The
NL7002 migration fix, which rewrote sites off `--unchecked-indexing`, goes
with the flag.

NL7001, NL7002, NL9014, NL9015 and NL2426 are retired. The tests,
cookbook entries and benchmark variants that existed only for the removed
forms are deleted, and the language reference, the user guide, the AI guide,
the FAQ, the architecture notes and the security records no longer describe
them.

BREAKING CHANGE: `Arena.release` and `Arena.reset` no longer compile, and
`--wrapping` and `--unchecked-indexing` exit 2.
Tests: arena_removed, tests/nish/cli.ts

* test(self): move the benches off the removed arena calls

The AWFY harness now lets innerBenchmarkLoop's automatic arena scope hand back each measurement instead of a manual block. The StringMap copy in bench/map-vs-stringmap.ts follows src/map.ts's reworded FNV comment again. The bench/cursor.ts advance positions move with its shorter comment.

Tests: bench, mem_awfy

* test(self): drop the arena blocks the checker refuses in six crypto suites

The crypto_aes, crypto_p256, crypto_sha256, crypto_sha512, crypto_x25519 and crypto_x509_malformed loops were moved from Arena.mark/release to using arena() blocks, which the escape analysis refuses: each loop calls a parser or hasher that keeps allocations in object fields. In p256 and x25519 the old release also freed the message t.fail had just kept. The loops now run unscoped.

Tests: crypto_aes, crypto_p256, crypto_sha256, crypto_sha512, crypto_x25519, crypto_x509_malformed

* test(self): keep mem_reclaim_guards' output the same under --emit-ts

The TypeScript runtime's Arena.mark() always answers 0, so the guard that
tested for 0 printed "empty" there while the native run printed r2. A mark is
never negative in either runtime, so the guard now tests for that, and the
call stays in place for the analysis the case pins.

Tests: tests/cases/mem_reclaim_guards

entries.title: add gzip, zlib and DEFLATE, and gzip HTTP responses
entries.body:
New standard-library modules, in pure Nish and written from the RFCs:
nish/compress/deflate (a raw DEFLATE compressor at levels 0 to 9, greedy at
1 to 3 and lazy at 4 to 9, each block the smallest of dynamic, fixed and
stored; a decompressor that answers an error code for every malformed stream
and never writes past its limit), nish/compress/gzip and nish/compress/zlib
(the RFC 1952 and RFC 1950 framings, one-shot and, for gzip, streaming with
GzipWriter and GzipReader) and nish/compress/checksum (CRC-32 by
slicing-by-8, Adler-32). Every compressor and decompressor allocates its
tables once and nothing per call.

nish/net/http-compress negotiates Accept-Encoding (q-values, identity, *)
and gzips a body with HttpCompressor; Http1Connection.acceptEncoding and
respondEncoded answer an HTTP/1.1 request in one call with Content-Encoding,
the compressed Content-Length and Vary set. Compression stays opt-in.
metrics: gzip -1 of a 5.2 KB JSON body 25.1 us, 1.58x libdeflate -1 at the same size (1890 vs 1888 bytes); -6 1.47x libdeflate -6; +-10 %
